result.instructions:
KiCad EDA tools for schematic capture, PCB layout, symbol/footprint libraries, and project management.

CRITICAL RULES:
- NEVER read, edit, or write KiCad files (.kicad_sch, .kicad_pcb, .kicad_sym, .kicad_mod, .kicad_pro) directly. All manipulation MUST go through these MCP tools.
- NEVER run kicad-cli commands directly. Use the export, ERC, and DRC tools provided by this server.
- When a tool returns an error, try different parameters or a different tool. Do NOT fall back to manual file editing.

START HERE (fetch one of these by name; do not search blind):
- See what is in a schematic: list_schematic_components
- Add a part (resistor, capacitor, IC, ...): place_component
- Connect pins to a net: wire_pins_to_net
- Check the schematic: run_erc
- See what is on the board: list_pcb_footprints
- Place or move a footprint: place_footprint, move_footprint
- Route: add_trace, add_via, autoroute_pcb
- Check the board: run_drc
- Push the schematic to the board: update_pcb_from_schematic
- Manufacturing output: export_gerbers
- Start a new project: create_project
- Anything else: search by what you want to do. There are 109 tools; these are the entry points, not the whole surface.

FILE ACCESS:
- These tools reach the filesystem through this server's own process, which already runs with the user's permissions. You do NOT need filesystem access, a connected folder, or any other permission from the host application to use them.
- NEVER ask the user to connect, add, or grant access to a folder. If you need a file, call the tool.
- Every path parameter takes an absolute path.

        project_path: Path to .kicad_pro file (for correct hierarchy resolution in sub-sheets)

        y1: Start Y
        x2: End X
        y2: End Y
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: remove_wire

tools.description:
Remove a junction at the given coordinates, as KiCad's delete removes one.

    The junction within 0.1 mm goes, with any other at exactly its point. Then, as KiCad's
    DeleteJunction does (bus-wire-junction.cpp:115-185 at 9.0.8), of the wires and buses
    ending there each parallel pair is made one, or one of two identical lines goes, so
    whatever met only at the junction is disconnected: a T loses its stem, a crossing becomes
    two wires that do not join. Wires that merely meet there at an angle stay joined. Where a
    bus entry ends at the point nothing is merged, since kicad-cli 9 cuts a wire at a bus entry
    end inside it. The result names each merge.

    Args:
        x: X position
        y: Y position
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: remove_junction

tools.description:
Add multiple wires at once, as KiCad's wire tool adds them. Each wire dict has keys:
    x1, y1, x2, y2.

    Following SCH_LINE_WIRE_BUS_TOOL::finishSegments (sch_line_wire_bus_tool.cpp:1168-1276 at
    9.0.8): a junction goes wherever three or more wire directions, pins or sheet pins meet,
    at a new wire's end or at a point already on the sheet that a new wire runs through (a
    pin, a wire end), and every wire through a junction is split there, so a T, or a wire
    drawn through a pin, joins in every reader. As KiCad merges the new wire with the
    collinear wires of its stroke that it overlaps or meets end to end (where no junction
    is), a stretch such a wire already covers is left out, and a merged run holding both
    pins of a two-pin part loses the stretch between them, so drawing across a part never
    shorts it. A wire of no length is left out, as KiCad's tool drops one. Existing wires
    are only ever split: where KiCad's trim would cut a wire already on the sheet, the call
    is refused and nothing is written. The result counts the wire nodes written and names
    each junction, split, left-out and trimmed stretch; when nothing changes it says so and
    writes nothing.

    Args:
        wires: List of wire defs [{x1, y1, x2, y2}, ...]
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: add_wires

tools.description:
Add a net label at a position.

    Args:
        text: Net name (e.g. "VIN_PROT", "5V_REL")
        x: X position
        y: Y position
        rotation: Degrees (0=right, 90=up, 180=left, 270=down)
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: add_label

tools.description:
Add multiple junctions, as KiCad's junction tool places them. Each point dict has
    keys: x, y.

    A junction joins only where three or more wire directions, pins or sheet pins meet: a
    crossing, a T, a wire end at a pin with another wire. Anywhere else (empty space, a
    straight wire's interior, an L corner, a wire ending at a pin) KiCad's editor refuses it,
    "Junction location contains no joinable wires and/or pins." (sch_drawing_tools.cpp:
    1465-1497 at 9.0.8), and its cleanup deletes one placed there, so the whole call is
    refused, naming each such point, and nothing is written. Every wire through a junction
    is split there, which kicad-cli 9 needs to read the join; where a junction is already
    exactly at a point no second one is added, but a wire still running through it is split.
    A point where KiCad allows a junction, or where one already is, is taken even off the
    page: it lies on wires or pins already drawn, which KiCad reads there as anywhere else.
    Any other point off the page is refused as off the page. The result names each junction
    written, each one already there and each split.

    Args:
        points: List of junction positions [{x, y}, ...]
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.

tools.description:
Move a placed component, turn it, or both.

    The symbol and all its fields move together: each field keeps its place relative to the
    symbol, rotation included, and keeps its own text angle, so KiCad draws it turning with
    the symbol. KiCad's GUI would also re-place auto-placed fields after a turn when its
    autoplace preference is on; this tool does not.

    Wires, labels, junctions and no-connect flags stay where they are, as with KiCad's own
    Move. The result lists every pin whose connections changed (what it left, what it now
    meets); reconnect those with wire_pins_to_net or connect_pins.

    x and y snap to the 1.27 mm grid when the symbol moves, and the grid point must lie on the
    page. Passing the symbol's own position (as list_schematic_components reports it) turns it in
    place without snapping, wherever it stands, off the page included. Nothing is written when
    nothing would change.

    Args:
        reference: Reference designator (e.g. "R1")
        x: New X position
        y: New Y position
        rotation: The absolute angle in degrees (None = keep current); a mirrored symbol keeps
            its mirror. It is written as KiCad writes it, so it also repairs an angle KiCad
            cannot load, such as 45, +90 or none; a call without it refuses one this tool
            cannot read as 0, 90, 180 or 270.
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: move_component

tools.description:
Set any property on a placed component, or rename it. Creates the
    property if it is missing.

    Reference, Value and Footprint are mirrored into the symbol's own
    instances and into the root symbol_instances table, so setting
    key="Reference" is how a component is renamed and both views stay in
    step. The root table needs the .kicad_pro to resolve the hierarchy
    path; a loose .kicad_sch with no project beside it keeps the symbol
    correct and leaves that table alone.

    Args:
        reference: Component reference (e.g. "R1")
        key: Property name (e.g. "MPN", "Tolerance", "Value")
        value: Property value
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: set_component_property

tools.description:

        height: Custom height in mm (required when size='User')
        portrait: If True, swap width/height for portrait orientation
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: set_page_size

tools.description:
Place a power symbol (VCC, GND, +3V3, etc.).

    Uses place_component internally. Power symbols are regular symbols
    from the 'power' library with isPower=True.

    Places only the symbol asked for. A PWR_FLAG tells ERC the net has a
    source it cannot see, which only the designer knows, so add one with
    lib_id="power:PWR_FLAG" on each net that needs it.

    Args:
        lib_id: Library ID (e.g. "power:VCC", "power:GND")
        reference: Reference (e.g. "#PWR01")
        x: X position
        y: Y position
        rotation: Rotation in degrees
        symbol_lib_path: Path to a .kicad_sym file that defines the power symbol,
            for a library outside KiCad's stock set. Optional; omit to load it
            from the stock library named by the lib_id prefix.
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
        project_path: Path to .kicad_pro file (for sub-sheet instance tracking)
tools.name: add_power_symbol

tools.description:
Place a decoupling capacitor and wire it to power/ground nets.

    Places the cap, wires pin 1 (top) to power_net and pin 2 (bottom)
    to ground_net via stub wires + labels.

    Args:
        lib_id: Cap symbol (e.g. "Device:C")
        reference: Reference (e.g. "C5")
        value: Cap value (e.g. "100nF")
        x: X position
        y: Y position
        power_net: Label for pin 1 (e.g. "VCC", "+3V3")
        ground_net: Label for pin 2 (e.g. "GND", "PGND")
        rotation: Rotation in degrees (default 0)
        symbol_lib_path: Path to a .kicad_sym file that defines the capacitor,
            for a library outside KiCad's stock set. Optional; omit to load it
            from the stock library named by the lib_id prefix.
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
        project_path: Path to .kicad_pro file (for sub-sheet instance tracking)
tools.name: auto_place_decoupling_cap

tools.description:
Add a text annotation to the schematic.

    Args:

        y: Y position
        rotation: Rotation in degrees
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: add_text

tools.description:
Remove text annotation(s) by content, optionally filtered by position.

    If x and y are provided, only removes texts matching both content AND

    Args:

        x: Optional X position filter
        y: Optional Y position filter
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: remove_text

tools.description:
Put each listed pin on the net named label_text, or refuse and write nothing.

    Each pin gets a short wire stub pointing away from its symbol, with a net
    label at the stub's end. When the stub would touch, overlap or cross
    anything else on the sheet, or move a net into another net class, the
    label goes on the pin end itself instead. No junction is ever written, and
    a pin already on the net is left alone. The file is written once or not
    at all.

    The whole call is refused when any pin cannot be wired safely: its net may
    already carry another name, it may reach something this tool cannot judge
    (a bus, a sheet pin, a text variable, a copy of the pad on another sheet),
    another part shares its reference, or every position is blocked. The
    refusal lists every refused pin with a bracketed reason code such as
    [names] or [touch], the obstacle, and a remedy. add_label and add_wires
    check none of this, so they are no way around a refusal.

    It places no PWR_FLAG: whether a net needs one depends on every driver on
    the net, not on the pins in one call. Use add_power_symbol for that.

    Args:
        pins: List of {"reference": "R1", "pin": "1"} dicts
        label_text: Net name (e.g. "GND", "VCC"), exactly as it should read: no surrounding
            spaces, no leading "/", no text variable ("${...}"), no bus syntax, not a KiCad
            auto name such as "Net-(R1-1)"
        direction: Stub direction: "auto" (away from the symbol), "left", "right", "up", "down"
        stub_length: Stub length in mm, a multiple of 1.27 up to 1000 (default 2.54)
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.

PinRefSpec.title: PinRefSpec

tools.name: wire_pins_to_net

tools.description:
Connect two component pins with Manhattan (L-shaped) wire routing.

    Combines get_pin_positions + coordinate math + add_wires into one call. At its own
    points (both pins and the L's corner) a junction goes where three or more directions
    meet, and any wire through it is split there, as KiCad's wire tool does
    (sch_line_wire_bus_tool.cpp:1263-1267 at 9.0.8); a leg running through a junction or a
    bus entry end already on the sheet is split there too, as KiCad's cleanup splits it. The
    result names each junction and split.

    Args:
        ref1: First component reference (e.g. "U1")
        pin1: First pin name or number
        ref2: Second component reference (e.g. "C3")
        pin2: Second pin name or number
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: connect_pins

tools.description:
Place a no-connect flag on a component pin.

    Resolves pin position and places a no-connect flag. Idempotent:
    calling again for a pin that already has one is a no-op.

    Args:
        reference: Component reference (e.g. "U2")
        pin_name: Pin name (e.g. "NC") or number (e.g. "3")
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: no_connect_pin

tools.description:
Remove no-connect flag(s) from a component pin.

    Removes every no-connect at the pin's position, so stacked
    duplicates from repeated no_connect_pin calls clear in one go.

    Args:
        reference: Component reference (e.g. "U2")
        pin_name: Pin name (e.g. "NC") or number (e.g. "3")
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: remove_no_connect

tools.description:
List unconnected pins by running ERC and filtering results.

    Requires kicad-cli. Lists the violations KiCad types pin_not_connected. A
    sub-sheet is checked from its project's root, as run_erc does, and gets
    the pins of that sheet alone, under every top-level sheet the project lists.
    A sheet below a top-level sheet other than the root is refused when that
    kicad-cli did not check it from the root. A run that makes no report
    raises and leaves output_dir as it was.

    The x and y of each entry are millimetres (mm) in sheet coordinates, the
    numbers get_pin_positions prints.

    Args:
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
        output_dir: Directory for ERC report file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
        project_path: Path to .kicad_pro file; the project whose hierarchy to look in.
            Refused when no sheet of it uses the file.
tools.name: list_unconnected_pins

tools.description:
Run Electrical Rules Check (ERC) on a schematic.

    A sub-sheet is checked from its project's root, so the hierarchy around it
    counts, and only that sheet's own violations are returned, those of every
    use of it under every top-level sheet the project lists. A sheet below a
    top-level sheet other than the root is refused when that kicad-cli did not
    check it from the root; run_erc on that top-level sheet checks it on its
    own. A file that no sheet of its project uses is checked on its own. A run
    that makes no report raises and leaves output_dir as it was.

    Returns JSON report with violations. An item's position is in
    millimetres (mm) in sheet coordinates, the numbers get_pin_positions prints.
    The report file saved in output_dir is kicad-cli's own.

    Args:
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
        output_dir: Directory for report file (default: beside the file ERC runs on).
            Optional; omit to use the configured default.
        project_path: Path to .kicad_pro file; the project whose hierarchy to look in.
            Refused when no sheet of it uses the file.
tools.name: run_erc

outputSchema.description:
ERC report. ``note`` carries any remarks, space-joined.

It is deliberately not single-purpose: it began as "ERC was redirected to
the root sheet" and now also explains a missing sym-lib-table. Test for the
remark you care about rather than for the field being empty.
outputSchema.title: ErcResult

tools.description:
Place a footprint on the PCB.

    Name a library and a footprint to place the real thing: its pads, silkscreen,
    courtyard and 3D model are copied from the library file exactly as KiCad
    would place them, a footprint in KiCad 7's form taking the reference and value
    in its own (fp_text reference|value ...), where one holding %V or %R, which KiCad
    reads there as a variable, is refused. Without them you get a marker carrying
    only the reference and value, which has NO PADS and so cannot be routed or
    checked; that is the older behaviour and it is kept for callers that only want a
    placeholder.

    Use list_lib_footprints to see what a library holds.

    The footprint is turned to its rotation as KiCad's own rotate turns it: every
    pad and text turns with it (a pad's angle is its library angle plus the
    footprint's), and a keep-upright text that would read upside down is turned
    half a turn with its justification mirrored, so it stays readable on the same
    side of its anchor. Angles are written as KiCad writes them: the footprint's
    between -180 and 180 and left out at 0, each pad's and text's absolute. Off the
    quarter turns the result reads as KiCad's placement without matching pcbnew's
    save byte for byte: footprint-relative coordinates stay as the library writes
    them where pcbnew re-derives them through two RotatePoint roundings, an fp_rect
    stays where pcbnew writes an fp_poly, and arc mid points stay as written. A
    library footprint without a Datasheet or Description field is placed without
    it, so KiCad reads that hidden field at its default on F.Fab, whereas pcbnew
    writes it, on B.Fab for a placement on the back.

    Zones the footprint owns (keepouts, say) and a KiCad 10 footprint's points are
    stored in board coordinates (format( ZONE ), pcb_io_kicad_sexpr.cpp:2628-2637 at
    9.0.8), so they land where KiCad's placement puts them: moved with the footprint,
    turned about it and, on the back, mirrored with it.

    A footprint carrying what this tool does not move with it (a dimension, image,
    table or barcode, or a child no KiCad it knows reads), or on the back what it does
    not flip (see move_footprint), is refused and nothing is written.

    Args:
        reference: Reference designator (e.g. "R2")
        value: Component value (e.g. "4.7K")
        x: X position in mm
        y: Y position in mm
        rotation: The footprint's angle in degrees, counter-clockwise as seen on
            screen; any finite value (270 is stored as -90, 360 as 0). inf and nan
            are refused and nothing is written.
        layer: F.Cu or B.Cu; any other layer is refused. B.Cu places the footprint
            flipped as KiCad's own flip does, then turns it to rotation
            (FOOTPRINT::Flip, pcbnew/footprint.cpp:2491-2550 at 9.0.8).
        library: Footprint library nickname (e.g. "Resistor_SMD"), or a path to a
            .pretty directory. A nickname is resolved as update_pcb_from_schematic
            resolves it: the project's fp-lib-table beside the board, .pretty
            directories beside the board, KICAD_FP_LIB, the user's global
            fp-lib-table (with the libraries the Plugin and Content Manager
            installed), then KiCad's stock footprints. Optional; omit for a
            pad-less marker.
        footprint: Footprint name within that library (e.g. "R_0805_2012Metric").
            Required when library is given.
        pcb_path: Path to .kicad_pcb file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: place_footprint

tools.description:
Move a footprint to a new position.

    A move rewrites the footprint's own position and nothing of its pads, texts
    or graphics, which KiCad stores relative to the footprint. The zones it owns
    and a KiCad 10 footprint's points are stored in board coordinates, so they
    move by the same delta, as KiCad's FOOTPRINT::SetPosition moves them
    (pcbnew/footprint.cpp:2553-2584 at 9.0.8). A rotation turns the footprint to
    that angle as KiCad's own rotate turns it: every pad and text turns by the
    change from the angle it had, its zones and points turn about it, and a
    keep-upright text that would read upside down is turned half a turn with its
    justification mirrored, so it stays readable on the same side of its anchor.
    Angles are written as KiCad writes them: the footprint's between -180 and 180
    and left out at 0. Off the quarter turns the result reads as KiCad's turn
    without matching pcbnew's save byte for byte: footprint-relative coordinates
    stay as written where pcbnew re-derives them through two RotatePoint roundings,
    an fp_rect stays where pcbnew writes an fp_poly, and arc mid points stay as
    written. A footprint carrying what this tool does not move with it
    (a dimension, image, table or barcode, or a child no KiCad it knows reads) is
    refused and nothing is written. The keep-out warning reads keepouts as
    check_placement does.

    Args:
        reference: Reference designator (e.g. "R1")
        x: New X position
        y: New Y position
        rotation: The footprint's angle after the move, in degrees (None keeps the
            current one). An angle the footprint already has (270 for one at -90,
            360 for one at 0) changes nothing and leaves the file byte-identical,
            where KiCad's footprint properties dialog would still re-run its
            rotate by a full turn. inf and nan are refused and nothing is written.
        layer: F.Cu or B.Cu (empty keeps the side; anything else is refused). The
            other side flips the footprint as KiCad's own flip does (FOOTPRINT::Flip,
            pcbnew/footprint.cpp:2491-2550 at 9.0.8): pads, texts and graphics
            mirror, their layers go to their opposites on this board (user layers it
            pairs included), a text's mirror toggles on side-specific layers only,
            zones and points mirror about the footprint with their layers, and 3D
            models stay as they are. With a rotation the flip comes first, so
            rotation names the angle the footprint ends at. Refused, with nothing
            written: a text box, a pad's own padstack, KiCad 10's back drills, and on
            a board of four or more copper layers an item (a zone included) on inner
            copper that does not name every inner layer, which KiCad 9 and 10 flip
            apart.
        pcb_path: Path to .kicad_pcb file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: move_footprint

    reads any other footprint layer; and the footprint's own keep-outs never
    count against it (intersectsArea skips an area whose parent is the item,
    pcbnew/pcbexpr_functions.cpp:697 at 9.0.8).

        x: Proposed X position
        y: Proposed Y position

tools.description:
Update the PCB from the schematic (headless Tools -> Update PCB from Schematic).

    Exports the schematic's netlist, loads the assigned footprints from
    libraries, and binds every pad to its net. Creates the .kicad_pcb if
    it does not exist; new footprints land in a grid cluster at orientation
    0, written as KiCad writes a footprint it has just loaded (no angle on the
    footprint, library pad and text angles normalized as KiCad holds them). Existing
    footprints are matched by reference and keep their position; a footprint in KiCad
    7's form, on the board or from its library, takes the symbol's reference and value
    in its (fp_text reference|value ...), and the update is refused when one holds %V or
    %R, which KiCad reads there as a variable. A changed
    footprint assignment swaps the footprint as KiCad's exchange does
    (pcbnew/pcb_edit_frame.cpp:2346-2587 at 9.0.8): it keeps its position,
    angle and side, its texts turned with it as the exchange turns them
    (SetOrientation, then on a KiCad 10 board KeepUpright on those it pairs
    with old ones), and its uuid, its pads' (by number; on a KiCad 10 board
    only a number each footprint holds once) and its fields' (by name), so a
    group still finds it. Off the quarter turns a swapped footprint reads as
    KiCad's exchange leaves it without matching pcbnew's save byte for byte:
    footprint-relative coordinates stay as the library writes them where
    pcbnew re-derives them through two RotatePoint roundings, an fp_rect stays
    where pcbnew writes an fp_poly, and arc mid points stay as written. A
    locked footprint is not swapped
    (skipped: footprint_locked), nor is one whose new footprint carries what
    this tool cannot move or flip (skipped: footprint_unsupported); either
    still takes the symbol's value, fields and nets. A new footprint carrying
    what this tool cannot move is not added (skipped: footprint_unsupported).
    Stale board footprints are reported, and removed only with delete_stale
    (a locked one, in any spelling KiCad reads, never is, and neither is one
    marked board only: KiCad's update keeps both). Zones are NOT refilled: run
    fill_zones afterward. Net names arrive exactly as KiCad's F8 produces them
    (local labels sheet-prefixed, e.g. "/SIG"); read them with list_pcb_nets.
    A pad whose net did not change is left as it is, and one that gains a net
    gets it where KiCad's writer puts it. A net that left the schematic goes to
    no net with everything on it, written as the board's format writes no net,
    unless a pad of a footprint that stays on the board is still on it (a stale
    footprint that is kept: delete_stale off, or locked, or board only); such a
    net keeps its row and everything on it. Segments, arcs and vias sent to no
    net are counted in orphaned_tracks, zones in orphaned_zones, and copper
    shapes are named in warnings. Nothing on a renamed net is moved to its new
    name: it goes to no net with the rest, or stays on the old net while a kept
    pad holds it.

    What KiCad's own update copies from the symbol follows it here, with
    two exceptions named below. The Value. Every other symbol field, as hidden
    text on the fabrication layer of the footprint's side: Datasheet and
    Description are updated where the library footprint put them, a new field
    is added at the footprint's origin at the footprint's own angle (mirrored
    on the back), and a field that left the symbol stays on the footprint
    (KiCad keeps a footprint's library fields the same way, and text the
    user may have placed is not an import's to remove). The symbol's
    footprint filters, as KiCad's (property ki_fp_filters ...). The DNP and
    "In BOM" boxes, set and cleared on the footprint's attributes; on a
    KiCad 10 netlist "Exclude from position files" too, while on KiCad 9,
    whose netlist has no such marker, that flag stays the board's own, as
    the mounting type, board_only and the courtyard choice always do. The
    sheet name and file, and the path that links the footprint to its
    symbol. A symbol with "On board" unticked is never placed and is listed
    in excluded_from_board; a footprint it left behind is reported stale like
    any other. Not copied: the Component Class field, which KiCad assigns as
    a component class rather than a field (dropped here), and KiCad 10's
    variant overrides, which are not applied. Existing footprints whose
    fields, filters, flags or sheet linkage moved are listed in
    fields_updated; a second run that changes nothing writes nothing.

    A footprint's library nickname is resolved the way KiCad resolves it:
    the project's own fp-lib-table first (beside the .kicad_pro, or beside
    the board or the schematic when none is named), then .pretty directories
    beside the board and the schematic, then KICAD_FP_LIB, then the user's
    global fp-lib-table together with the libraries the Plugin and Content
    Manager installed, then KiCad's stock footprints. ${KIPRJMOD}, the
    variables of Preferences > Configure Paths (kicad_common.json), the
    ${KICAD*_3RD_PARTY} and ${KICAD*_FOOTPRINT_DIR} families and the other
    KiCad path variables expand as KiCad expands them: the environment
    first, then the configured value, then KiCad's own default. A nickname
    none of those know is reported in skipped as footprint_lib_not_found.
    place_footprint resolves through the same code, so a hand-placed part
    and an imported one resolve to the same file.

    Requires kicad-cli. It no longer needs KiCad's pcbnew Python bindings.

    Every byte this writes goes through the server's byte-preserving write, so
    a board's format stamp does not move and the parts of it this tool did not
    touch arrive unchanged.

    Args:
        schematic_path: Path to .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
        pcb_path: Path to .kicad_pcb file (created if missing).
            Optional; omit to use the configured default.
        delete_stale: Remove unlocked board footprints absent from the schematic, except
            those marked board only
        project_path: Path to .kicad_pro for explicit root resolution (sub-sheets)

tools.description:

    directory.  kicad-cli has no per-footprint option here, and a single
    .kicad_mod path is rejected. So is a library that is, or holds, a link or
    anything other than plain files and folders, before anything is copied.

    KiCad performs the migration, as it should, but it performs it on a copy and
    each result lands through the server's atomic write, so no footprint file can
    be left truncated. Only files whose content actually changed are written, so
    an upgrade that touches three footprints leaves the rest of the library
    alone. The whole library is still copied to ``<name>.pretty.bak`` first and
    the result names it, because that is the undo for an upgrade that SUCCEEDED.
    There is exactly one, and every run overwrites it.

    interrupted midway leaves some footprints migrated and some not, and no file
    damaged. Version control is still the better answer for a library you care

tools.description:
Validate a hierarchical schematic for common issues.

    Checks every sheet below the root, however deep, each file once. A relative sheet file
    name is found beside the file holding the sheet, as KiCad finds it; a sheet that contains
    itself, which KiCad refuses, is skipped. Per sheet block: orphaned labels and pins,
    direction mismatches, a missing file, a file that cannot be parsed ("unreadable_file",
    whose "note" names the file; its checks are skipped, the rest still run). Per sheet
    instance, so a reused sheet counts once per use: duplicate and unannotated reference
    designators, each read from the entry KiCad reads at that instance, the root's
    symbol_instances table on a root in KiCad 6's form, else the symbol's own (the units of
    one multi-unit part share theirs); an instance with no entry reads the symbol's first
    entry, else its Reference property. Past 4096 instances a "references_unchecked" note says
    the rest went unchecked. Per file: the points where kicad-cli 9 drops part of a line that
    KiCad's editor keeps.

    Those are a junction strictly inside a wire or bus ("junction_inside_wire") and, in a file
    kicad-cli 9 loads, a bus entry end strictly inside one ("bus_entry_inside_wire"); KiCad's
    editor never saves either, and earlier versions of this package wrote both. kicad-cli 9
    (ERC, netlist export, PCB update) cuts the line there: per line, "kept" is the stretch it
    keeps and "dropped" the stretch it loses, cutting off whatever joins the line only along
    that. "editor" says what KiCad 9's editor makes of it: it splits the line, keeping a
    junction where three or more directions meet ("keeps_junction"), deleting it elsewhere
    ("deletes_junction"), and at a bus entry end placing none ("splits_wire"). A file stamped
    past KiCad 9's format gets neither reading. The readings follow KiCad's source; whether
    kicad-cli 9 loads the sheet at all is not checked. To fix one, make the call in its
    "repair" as given: add_junctions at the point, which splits the line, or remove_junction.
    Such an issue carries a "note" in place of a repair in two cases only: its sheet is one the
    connectivity model refuses (a symbol or pin at an angle KiCad cannot load; no reading
    either), or it is a bus entry end where KiCad allows no junction.

    Per file too: the no-connect flags ("no_connect_off_pin") and wire ends
    ("wire_end_off_pin") at the point releases 0.5.8 to 0.20.1 gave a pin of a symbol at
    rotation 90 or 270 with a mirror. They mirrored before rotating, so that point is the
    pin's end reflected through the symbol's origin, and 0.20.1's no_connect_pin,
    wire_pins_to_net and connect_pins wrote there (measured). Only a point where KiCad draws
    no pin is checked. Each issue names the symbol ("reference"), the "pin", the point ("x",
    "y") and where KiCad draws the pin ("pin_x", "pin_y"), and a wire end its "wire". Where
    the old transform put several pins at the point, the issue lists them under "pins" in
    place of those four, with a note and no repair, since which pin the flag or wire was
    written for is not known. A flag is not reported where a sheet pin or a hierarchical label
    is too; a wire end is not where an end of another item but a bus's lies on it, a flag and
    the Net-(<ref>-<pin>) label connect_pins wrote there apart; neither is where any reader
    may join it to a pin KiCad draws for the point already. A flag carries a note: no tool
    removes one by its position, so delete it in KiCad's editor, then no_connect_pin flags the
    pin. A wire end's "repair" is wire_pins_to_net with the one local label name on its net
    that the tool accepts, planned first; else a note, with the plan's refusal or, where the
    net has no single such name, the pin the wire reaches. Nothing is written.

    Args:
        schematic_path: Path to root .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
tools.name: validate_hierarchy

Put hierarchical sheets in the page order given: sheets listed come first, in that order,
    then the others in the order they have now.

    KiCad orders sheets by their page numbers, not by where their blocks sit in the file, so
    this rewrites the page numbers and leaves the blocks where they are. Call it on the root

    refused. The numbers already in use are given back in the new order, so custom labels
    such as "Intro" stay; when they repeat, or a deeper sheet uses one, the sheets are numbered
    from the lowest positive whole number no other sheet holds. A sheet whose instance entry
    was written at its own path, as earlier versions of the tools did, has it moved to the path

    again when the source's were autoplaced, and its page the lowest number no sheet uses,
    stored at the parent's path where KiCad reads it. The copied file's symbols get references
    of their own, so the two sheets are two sets of parts: each prefix takes its first free
    number across the hierarchy, in the order of the symbols' x then y position, and the
    units of one part keep one reference. A reference with no number stays as it is.

    A source file that holds sheets of its own is refused, with nothing written, because its
    sub-sheets would need new instance paths in other files. Give project_path when the
    parent is itself a sub-sheet, so its place in the hierarchy can be found.

tools.description:
Flatten a hierarchical schematic into a single sheet whose netlist is the hierarchy's.

    The flat file is the root schematic with each sub-sheet's content copied below it, one
    cell per use of a sheet file (a file used twice is copied twice). Each part keeps the
    reference and unit KiCad reads for it at its sheet's path. A sheet pin becomes a
    local label at its place when its sheet has a hierarchical label of its name, and nothing
    otherwise. A local or hierarchical label of a sub-sheet becomes a local label named after
    the sheet's path, so nets keep their joins and no others; net names change to those
    labels. A label whose own sheet has a global label, a power symbol or a hidden power input
    pin of its text keeps that text, so it keeps joining it. Text variables that name the
    sheet are not rewritten.

    The tool refuses, writing nothing, where the flat file could not keep the netlist: a
    sheet pin or sub-sheet label that may be a bus, a file older than format 20221002, a
    local power symbol, a bus_alias in a sub-sheet, a root label named like a global net
    that only another sheet has, a library symbol whose pins differ between two files, a
    sheet marked DNP, out of the BOM, off the board or out of simulation,
    two sheets of one name, more than 4096 sheet instances, or a sheet file that cannot be
    read. A sheet file that is missing is flattened as an empty sheet, as KiCad loads it.

    Creates a new file and does not modify the hierarchy.

    Args:
        schematic_path: Path to root .kicad_sch file. Optional; omit to use the configured default.
        output_path: Path for flattened output (defaults to *_flat.kicad_sch)
